standard_prerequisites.use: Turns normality of the normalization into geometric regularity and hence smoothness.

core_obligations: Reduce first to X reduced and then, using the reduced projective completion lemma, to X projective (proof lines 9329-9334).

Let Y be the normalization of the completion and conclude that Y is geometrically regular because normal and regular agree in dimension at most one, hence Y is smooth over the (separable) base (proof lines 9342-9346).
Decompose Y into irreducible components Y_i and show that each ring of global sections is a finite separable extension of the base field (proof lines 9347-9351).
Conclude the existence of the required commutative diagram with smooth projective geometrically irreducible pieces by the Stein factorization lemma (proof line 9352).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the reduced projective case.
Pass to the normalization and use regularity in dimension one for smoothness.
Decompose into components with separable function fields.
Apply the factorization lemma to finish.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, after a finite separable extension of the ground field, a commutative diagram completing a separated finite type scheme of dimension at most one by smooth projective geometrically irreducible curves over separable extensions of the base. The proof reduces to the projective case using the reduced completion lemma, lets Y be the normalization of the projective completion, and observes that Y is geometrically regular because normality and regularity agree in dimension at most one, so Y is smooth over the (separable) base; the irreducible components Y_i then have finite separable fields of global sections and the conclusion follows by an application of the Stein factorization lemma (proof lines 9328-9352). H3: the combination of the normalization, the regularity-in-dimension-one fact and the Stein factorization step is independent work.
